subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve agent harnesses across empty-plugin-scope reloads

question: When a gateway reload resolves to an explicit empty plugin scope, should plugin-owned harnesses be removed, should only a documented always-on core class remain, or should the reload avoid replacing unrelated active plugin state altogether?
rationale: The answer determines whether restoring all previous harnesses is a compatibility fix or a lifecycle leak; source and production discussion show both bundled and third-party plugin behavior are affected.

options.title: Preserve active registry ownership
options.body: Adopt the scoped-load merge approach so only missing requested plugins are registered and unrelated active plugin lifecycles are not torn down.

options.title: Keep only explicit always-on harnesses
options.body: Introduce a narrowly defined ownership class for core provider harnesses and retain only that class across an empty scope.

options.title: Treat empty scope as authoritative teardown
options.body: Keep empty scope as a full removal and pursue the upstream cause of unexpected empty-scope reloads instead.

recommendation.title: Preserve active registry ownership
recommendation.body: Adopt the scoped-load merge approach so only missing requested plugins are registered and unrelated active plugin lifecycles are not torn down.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current loader rollback boundary that this decision must extend or preserve.
